cards.prose: Count the men he has just called and count the tribes, and it comes out twelve and twelve. Here he says what the match is for. The men who have followed him will sit on *twelve thrones*, and what they judge is all the tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), not one house of it. The sending in Matthew is the first of that work.
cards.member_phrase: ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) promises the men who followed him twelve thrones over the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel), which is why there are twelve of them.

cards.prose: Luke puts the same promise at the supper table on the night before the cross. The men who share his table in the kingdom are the men who sit on thrones over the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel). He sent them out with power in Matthew, and this is where the road was always headed for them.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: At the last supper he promises the same men a place at his table in the kingdom and thrones over the twelve tribes.

cards.prose: Matthew lists the twelve by name. At the end of the story the names of twelve apostles of the Lamb are set in the foundations of the city wall. The men he sent out with power were no passing crew, since they are part of what the city stands on.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb are set in the twelve foundations of the city wall.

cards.prose: The men he calls here are sent to *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Matthew 10:6), and the city at the end is built around those same tribes, with a name on each of the twelve gates. What the twelve go out to gather is what the gates are named for.
cards.member_phrase: names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: The twelve gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, the same tribes the twelve are sent to.

cards.prose: Matthew counts twelve men. Revelation counts a sealed company drawn *of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)*. It is the same people in both, a people named by its tribes. The twelve are sent out to them, and in the end they are sealed.
cards.member_phrase: sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel)
cards.member_sentence: A hundred and forty-four thousand are sealed from all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel), counted by tribe.

cards.prose: The tribes the twelve are sent to gather are headed somewhere. Ezekiel is shown the house restored, and *waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward*. The vision of the tribes in their land has this house at its center, with the water running out from it.
cards.member_phrase: waters issued out from under the threshold of the house eastward
cards.member_sentence: Ezekiel sees water running out from under the threshold of the restored house, the place the gathered tribes are brought to.
cards.flag: This verse is the river from the house; it does not itself name the tribes (the allotment to the twelve tribes comes later in the chapter), so the old note's point is carried by the vision as a whole.

cards.prose: He said this to the crowd on the mountain, and here he gives the twelve the same teaching in walking shoes. What is holy is not pressed on those who trample it. When a house will not hear, the twelve shake off the dust and go on, and they do not chase a hearing that has been refused.
cards.member_phrase: neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet
cards.member_sentence: On the mountain he teaches that what is holy is not pressed on those who trample it.

cards.prose: The whole city came out, saw him, and asked him to leave, and he went. He did not force himself on them. That is the pattern he gives the twelve for any town that *shall not receive you*. They say what they were sent to say, and if it is refused they go.
cards.member_phrase: they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts
cards.member_sentence: A whole city asks him to leave its coasts, and he leaves, which is the pattern for the twelve.

cards.prose: Years later Paul and Barnabas do just what he told the twelve. They shake off the dust and *came unto Iconium*. It is no retreat, since the verse ends with them arriving in the next city. The sheep are scattered, and when one door shuts they go on looking for the ones who will hear.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul and Barnabas shake off the dust against a city and go on to Iconium.

cards.prose: At Corinth the synagogue turned on Paul and spoke against him, so he shook out his clothes and said *I am clean*. He had said what he came to say. The turning to the Gentiles is a change of door, since Paul's field was the scattered house of Yashar'el (Israel) living out among the nations, and the same Shepherd is looking for them there.
cards.member_phrase: I am clean: from henceforth I will go unto the Gentiles
cards.member_sentence: At Corinth Paul shakes out his raiment when the synagogue blasphemes, and turns to the Gentiles.
cards.flag: Reads Paul's Gentiles at Corinth as the scattered house among the nations, per the teaching; the old note did not say so.

cards.prose: To say how a refused city will fare he points to Sodom, and Sodom's end is right here: *brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven*. Then he says Sodom will have it lighter in the day of judgment than the town that would not hear the men he sent. A refused word weighs more than a city that was burned.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Sodom's end, fire and brimstone from Yahuah (the LORD) out of heaven, is the measure he sets against the town that refuses.

cards.prose: Matthew lists them and Mark says how they became twelve. He went up into a mountain and called *whom he would*, and *they came unto him*. The twelve were picked by him and not by their own asking, and the power in Matthew's verse was given to men he had chosen first.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Mark shows him going up a mountain and calling the twelve to himself, whom he would, and they came.

cards.prose: Before the names there was a night. Luke has him on the mountain *all night in prayer to Elohim (God)* before he called anyone. The twelve Matthew lists were chosen only after he had spent the night in prayer.
cards.member_phrase: went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to Elohim (God)
cards.member_sentence: Luke has him pray all night on the mountain before he chooses the twelve.

cards.prose: Set the two lists side by side and the same men are in both, with one gone. Matthew ends his list on Judas Iscariot, who betrayed him, and the room in Acts holds eleven names. The twelve were sent out with power, and the gap shows that one of them did not stay with it.
cards.member_phrase: and Thomas, Bartholomew, and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James
cards.member_sentence: After the resurrection eleven of the men are named in the upper room, with the place of the one who betrayed him empty.

cards.prose: The reach he gives the twelve is the reach he states to the woman crying after him: *the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel)*. She is not sent away in the end, since her daughter is healed, and her coast is the very ground where the scattered house was swallowed up. She is one of the sheep he said he was sent to.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He tells the woman of Canaan the same scope he gave the twelve, the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).
cards.flag: Reads the woman of Canaan as one of the scattered house, as the teaching does; the old note only named the matching scope.

cards.prose: Paul's order is the order Yahusha (Jesus) gave the twelve: *to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek*. First the house in the land, then the same scattered house out among the Greeks. He is not naming two kinds of people there, only two places where the lost sheep are found.
cards.member_phrase: to every one that believeth; to the Yahudi (Jew) first, and also to the Greek
cards.member_sentence: Paul keeps the order of the sending, the Yahudi (Jew) first and then the Greek, the house in the land and then the scattered house abroad.

cards.prose: Paul says in his own words what the sending says. Yahusha (Jesus) came to the circumcision, the sons of the fathers, so that what was promised to the fathers would be made good. The twelve go to the house of Yashar'el (Israel) because that is where the promise was aimed.
cards.member_phrase: was a minister of the circumcision for the truth of Elohim (God), to confirm the promises made unto the fathers
cards.member_sentence: Paul says Yahusha (Jesus) was a minister of the circumcision to confirm the promises made to the fathers.

cards.prose: The things he tells the twelve to do were already written in Isaiah as the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes and saves. *The eyes of the blind shall be opened*, the prophet says. When the twelve heal, they carry what Isaiah said would mark that day.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah foretells the eyes of the blind opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped when Elohim (God) comes to save.

cards.prose: John sent his disciples to ask whether he was the one who should come. Yahusha (Jesus) answered with a list, and it is the list he has just handed the twelve: *the lepers are cleansed*, *the dead are raised up*. What he gave John for an answer is the work he gives them to do.
cards.member_phrase: the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them
cards.member_sentence: Yahusha (Jesus) answers John's question with the same works he has just given the twelve power to do.

cards.prose: *Freely ye have received, freely give.* Simon saw the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) given by the laying on of hands and *offered them money*. He wanted to buy what the twelve were told to hand out for nothing. Peter will not take it, and the gift stays what it was, not for sale.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Simon offers money for the gift of the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), the one thing the twelve were told to give freely.

cards.prose: Mark gives the same instruction almost word for word, and he adds what the dust is for: *a testimony against them*. Shaking it off is a witness that the word was brought to that town and refused. Like Matthew, Mark ends the verse on Sodom.
cards.member_phrase: shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them
cards.member_sentence: Mark gives the same instruction and names what the dust is for, a testimony against that town, with Sodom set beside it.

cards.prose: Luke has the same instruction, and he marks the place for it. The dust comes off *when ye go out of that city*, on the way out. It is done quietly, and what is left behind is a testimony.
cards.member_phrase: shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them
cards.member_sentence: Luke has the same instruction, with the dust shaken off as they leave the city, for a testimony against it.

cards.prose: He says it again over Capernaum, a town that had seen his works. If those *mighty works* had been done in Sodom, he says, it would still be standing. The more a town has been shown, the more it answers for, and that is what the twelve are told about the town that will not receive them.
cards.member_phrase: if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day
cards.member_sentence: Capernaum is told it will answer for more than Sodom, because Sodom never saw the works done there.

cards.prose: The dove in Noah's story came back in the evening with an olive leaf, and that told Noah the waters were going down. A dove carries news and does no harm. When Yahusha (Jesus) says *harmless as doves*, that is the kind of bearing he describes for the twelve as they go among wolves.
cards.member_phrase: in her mouth was an olive leaf pluckt off: so Noah knew that the waters were abated from off the earth
cards.member_sentence: A dove brings Noah an olive leaf and the news that the waters are going down.

cards.prose: At the Jordan the Spirit came down on Yahusha (Jesus) *like a dove*. So the dove he tells the twelve to be like is the dove that rested on him at the start of his own work. The harmlessness he asks of them is what he carried himself.
cards.member_phrase: he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him
cards.member_sentence: The Spirit of Elohim (God) comes down on Yahusha (Jesus) like a dove at his baptism.

cards.prose: He says the same words again when he speaks about the last days: *endure unto the end*. They were spoken first to men about to be sent out, and they are spoken again about the end itself, so the same road runs the whole way from this sending to that day.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The same promise is spoken again in his words on the last days: the one who endures to the end is saved.

cards.prose: Mark gives the same pair in the same order. First comes the hatred, *hated of all men for my name's sake*, and only then the one who endures. The saying is a promise to people who are already being hated, and it is put to them as the way through.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Mark pairs being hated for his name with the one who endures to the end being saved.

cards.prose: Where Matthew says the one who endures to the end is saved, Hebrews says we are *made partakers of Messiah (Christ), if* we hold what we began with *stedfast unto the end*. Sharing in him is tied to holding on, so the end is where it shows who held.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews says we share in Messiah (Christ) if we hold our first confidence steadfast to the end.

cards.prose: Endure is spelled out here as patience, and patience has an aim. Ye *have need of patience* so that, once the will of Elohim (God) is done, the promise is received. The saving he promises the one who endures is that promise, received at the end of the doing.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Hebrews says patience is needed so that, after the will of Elohim (God) is done, the promise is received.

cards.prose: When he speaks of the Son of Adam coming, he is using Daniel's picture: *one like the Son of Adam* came *with the clouds of heaven* and was brought near before the Ancient of days. The coming that sets the limit on the twelve going over the cities is the coming Daniel saw.
cards.member_phrase: one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days
cards.member_sentence: Daniel sees one like the Son of Adam come with the clouds of heaven to the Ancient of days.

cards.prose: *Till the Son of Adam be come* is the clock on the sending, and here is the coming itself: *coming in the clouds of heaven*. The cities of Yashar'el (Israel) are gone over until that day, and when it comes the tribes of the earth mourn.
cards.member_phrase: they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam is seen coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory, and the tribes of the earth mourn.

cards.prose: Here the same coming has a reward attached, and the reward goes by works: he will *reward every man according to his works*. So the twelve are sent through the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) until the day he comes in the glory of his Father and weighs what each one did.
cards.member_phrase: the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels
cards.member_sentence: The Son of Adam comes in his Father's glory with his angels and rewards every man according to his works.

cards.prose: The fire in Isaiah's last verse has dead bodies in front of it, the *carcases* of those who transgressed. That is the picture under his word about the one who can *destroy both soul and body*. The worm and the fire do not stop, and what they work on is already dead.
cards.member_phrase: their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched
cards.member_sentence: Isaiah ends on the dead bodies of the transgressors, with the worm and the fire that do not stop.

cards.prose: The word behind *hell* in his sentence is the valley of Hinnom, and this is what Jeremiah says went on there: they built the high places of Tophet to *burn their sons and their daughters in the fire*, which Yahuah (the LORD) says he never commanded. His hearers knew that place by its history.
cards.member_phrase: built the high places of Tophet, which is in the valley of the son of Hinnom, to burn their sons and their daughters in the fire
cards.member_sentence: Jeremiah names Tophet in the valley of Hinnom, where sons and daughters were burned in the fire.

cards.prose: Josiah put an end to it. He *defiled Topheth* so that no man could pass his son or daughter through the fire to Molech. A king had to defile the place to stop the burning, so the valley his hearers knew as a defiled place is the one he points to when he says destroy.
cards.member_phrase: he defiled Topheth, which is in the valley of the children of Hinnom
cards.member_sentence: Josiah defiles Topheth in the valley of Hinnom so that no one can pass his son or daughter through the fire to Molech.

cards.prose: Revelation gives the end of that road a name, *the second death*. He calls it death, and the only one the twelve are told to fear is the one who can bring it. The men who kill the body can do nothing to this.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Death and hell are cast into the lake of fire, and John calls it the second death.

cards.prose: Fear is a strange word to hear after *fear not*, but he sets one fear that drives out the rest. Proverbs puts the fear of Yahuah (the LORD) at *the beginning of wisdom*, so what he points the twelve toward is where understanding starts, and not a dread that makes them run.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The fear of Yahuah (the LORD) is the beginning of wisdom, and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.

cards.prose: Luke has the same saying with the Son of Adam doing the confessing. Whoever *shall confess me before men* will be confessed *before the angels of Elohim (God)*. Matthew says before my Father in heaven and Luke says before the angels, and either way the answer to a confession made on earth is spoken in heaven.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke says whoever confesses him before men, the Son of Adam will confess before the angels of Elohim (God).

cards.prose: Paul gives it as a pair: *if we suffer, we shall also reign with him*, and *if we deny him, he also will deny us*. The hatred and the cost Matthew warns of are on the road to the reign, and the one who denies him is answered in kind.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Paul says that if we suffer we reign with him, and if we deny him he will deny us.

cards.prose: Confessing him before men is more than saying his name. On the mountain he says *not every one that saith* Adonai (Lord) goes into the kingdom, only the one who *doeth the will of my Father*. The confession he answers is one that is lived out.
cards.member_phrase: but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Saying Adonai (Lord) is not enough; the one who enters the kingdom is the one who does the Father's will.

cards.prose: He is quoting. Micah's words are almost his own, *a man's enemies are the men of his own house*, so the household breaking apart is nothing new with him. The prophet saw it long before the sending.
cards.member_phrase: a man’s enemies are the men of his own house
cards.member_sentence: Micah says a man's enemies are the men of his own house, the words Yahusha (Jesus) takes up.

cards.prose: Luke says plainly what the sword is. He did not come *to give peace on earth* but *rather division*. Matthew's picture of a blade and Luke's word are one thing, a line drawn through households with a man's own family on either side of it.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke records him saying he did not come to give peace on earth but division.

cards.prose: The enmity in a household goes back to the first word spoken after the serpent, enmity between *thy seed and her seed*. There were two seeds from the beginning, and the line between them can run through a family, which is how a man's foes come to sit at his own table.
cards.member_phrase: between thy seed and her seed; it shall bruise thy head, and thou shalt bruise his heel
cards.member_sentence: Yahuah (the LORD) puts enmity between the serpent's seed and the woman's seed, the first division.

cards.prose: None of this cancels the fifth commandment. *Honour thy father and thy mother* stands, and loving him above them is an order of loves, not a setting aside of what Yahuah (the LORD) commanded. When a house divides, it divides over who he is, and the commandment is still the commandment.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The fifth commandment stands: honour thy father and thy mother, and the promise of long days on the land goes with it.

cards.prose: The saying comes back after Peter's confession, and nothing in it is softened. Here it is put as an invitation, and it gains a line: *deny himself*. The cross he mentions to the twelve before they go is the same cross he tells all his disciples to take up after him.
cards.member_phrase: let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me
cards.member_sentence: After Peter's confession he tells his disciples to deny themselves, take up the cross, and follow.

cards.prose: Mark shows who else was listening. He *called the people unto him with his disciples also*. In Matthew the saying is spoken to the twelve as they are sent, and in Mark the crowd is called in to hear it, so it was no secret of the inner circle.
cards.member_phrase: let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me
cards.member_sentence: Mark has him call the crowd in with his disciples to hear that anyone who follows must take up his cross.

cards.prose: Luke says it to *them all* and puts *daily* in front of the cross. What he tells the twelve at the sending is not one hour of courage but the way each day goes for the one who follows.
cards.member_phrase: let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me
cards.member_sentence: Luke adds that the cross is taken up daily, and says it to them all.

cards.prose: Luke states the other side, as Matthew does at the end of the verse. Without the cross he says the man *cannot be my disciple*. It is a plain condition of following him, and Luke follows it at once with a man sitting down to count the cost.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: Luke says the one who does not bear his cross and come after him cannot be his disciple.

cards.prose: *He that findeth his life shall lose it.* The man who stores up for himself on earth has found his life in what moth and rust can eat. Yahusha (Jesus) told the crowd on the mountain the same, *treasures upon earth*, and finding and losing again turns on where the treasure is.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: He tells the crowd not to lay up treasures on earth where moth and rust corrupt and thieves steal.
cards.flag: The old note's watcher-rebellion line is dropped; the pair is read as finding and losing a life turning on where the treasure lies.

cards.prose: This psalm opens by calling *all ye people* to hear before it speaks of wisdom. What it goes on to speak of is the man who trusts in what he has gathered and the life that no riches can hold. His saying about finding a life and losing it is that old saying said again.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: The psalm opens by calling every person in the world to listen before it speaks of wisdom.
cards.flag: Verse 1 is only the call to listen; the pair rests on the psalm as a whole (wealth cannot ransom a life), which the packet's context does not show.

cards.prose: Matthew sets the chain of receiving at the sending out, and John sets it at the table later, in the same shape. Receive the one he sends and you receive him, and receive him and you receive *him that sent me*.
cards.member_phrase: WHOLE
cards.member_sentence: John records the same chain: whoever receives the one he sends receives him, and whoever receives him receives the one who sent him.

cards.prose: The same pattern is carried to the judgment. What is done for *the least of these my brethren* is counted as done for him. Here the receiving is traced to the end, so a welcome given to someone he sent is reckoned on the last day as given to him.
cards.member_phrase: Inasmuch as ye have done it unto one of the least of these my brethren, ye have done it unto me
cards.member_sentence: What is done to one of the least of his brethren he counts as done to himself.

cards.prose: Set the cup of cold water beside alms given *to be seen of them*. One has no reward from the Father, and the other is only a drink of water in a disciple's name, and it will *in no wise lose* its reward. He weighs the gift by the heart behind it.
cards.member_phrase: to be seen of them: otherwise ye have no reward of your Father which is in heaven
cards.member_sentence: Alms given before men to be seen have no reward from the Father, the opposite of the cup of water given quietly.

cards.prose: The reward that shall not be lost has a place at the end of the road, a kingdom *prepared for you from the foundation of the world*. The King calls those on his right hand *ye blessed of my Father*. The cup of water is not the price of that kingdom. It is one of the small things he does not let drop.
cards.member_phrase: Come, ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world
cards.member_sentence: At the judgment the King calls the sheep blessed and gives them the kingdom prepared from the foundation of the world.

new_threads.title: The twelve he calls, and the twelve tribes they are set over
new_threads.summary_md:
Matthew counts his men before he sends them. They are twelve, called to him and given power.

*And when he had called unto him his twelve disciples, he gave them power against unclean spirits, to cast them out, and to heal all manner of sickness and all manner of disease.* (Matthew 10:1)

The number matches something. Yahusha (Jesus) tells these same men what it is for, once on the road and once at the table.

*Verily I say unto you, That ye which have followed me, in the regeneration when the Son of Adam shall sit in the throne of his glory, ye also shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 19:28)

*That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Luke 22:30)

Twelve men for twelve tribes. That is why the errand is to the lost sheep of those same tribes, wherever they have been scattered.

*But go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Matthew 10:6)

The count is kept to the end of the story. The people sealed in Revelation are counted by tribe, and the city has the tribes on its gates and the apostles in its foundations.

*And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Revelation 7:4)

*And had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Yashar'el (Israel):* (Revelation 21:12)

*And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and in them the names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.* (Revelation 21:14)

The choosing was his before the sending was. Mark shows him going up the mountain and picking them himself, and Luke shows him spending the night in prayer first.

*And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.* (Mark 3:13)

So the twelve are men he chose, for a people he named, to judge a people he is gathering, and the city at the end carries both sets of names.

new_threads.title: Heal the sick, and give freely what was freely given
new_threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The works Yahusha (Jesus) puts in the hands of the twelve were written down by Isaiah as the signs of the day Elohim (God) comes to save.

*Heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, cast out devils: freely ye have received, freely give.* (Matthew 10:8)

Isaiah spoke to people with fearful hearts and told them who was coming.

*Say to them that are of a fearful heart, Be strong, fear not: behold, your Elohim (God) will come with vengeance, even Elohim (God) with a recompence; he will come and save you.* (Isaiah 35:4)

*Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5)

Yahusha (Jesus) reads from the same list when John sends to ask whether he is the one who should come.

*The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5)

So when the twelve heal, they are not doing something new. They carry the sign the prophet gave, and the sign points back to the one who sent them.

The gift also goes out the way it came in. Nobody paid for it, so nobody is to be charged for it. Simon saw the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) given and tried to buy his way in.

*And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit) was given, he offered them money,* (Acts 8:18)

The words in Matthew leave no room for that. What was received freely is given freely.

new_threads.title: Shake off the dust, and the day Sodom is measured against
new_threads.summary_md:
The twelve are told what to do with a town that will not have them.

*And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear your words, when ye depart out of that house or city, shake off the dust of your feet.* (Matthew 10:14)

It is the same teaching he gave the crowd, now with the men who must live it.

*Give not that which is holy unto the dogs, neither cast ye your pearls before swine, lest they trample them under their feet, and turn again and rend you.* (Matthew 7:6)

He had shown them how it is done. A whole city saw him and sent him away, and he went.

*And, behold, the whole city came out to meet Yahusha (Jesus): and when they saw him, they besought him that he would depart out of their coasts.* (Matthew 8:34)

The twelve do not follow after a hearing that is refused, and they do not stay to fight over it. Paul and Barnabas do the same, and the verse ends with them on the road to the next city.

*But they shook off the dust of their feet against them, and came unto Iconium.* (Acts 13:51)

The sending is broad because the sheep are scattered, and the dust is shaken only where the word has been heard and turned away. Then comes the weight of it. He sets a refused town against Sodom.

*Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.* (Matthew 10:15)

Sodom's end is written plainly.

*Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven;* (Genesis 19:24)

He says the same over Capernaum.

*And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted unto heaven, shalt be brought down to hell: for if the mighty works, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained until this day.* (Matthew 11:23)

A town that has been shown the works and the word answers for more than the one that burned. The measure is how much was shown.

new_threads.title: Until the Son of Adam be come
new_threads.summary_md:
*It ain't new.* The coming that Yahusha (Jesus) sets as the limit of the twelve's going was in Daniel before he ever spoke of it.

*But when they persecute you in this city, flee ye into another: for verily I say unto you, Ye shall not have gone over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel), till the Son of Adam be come.* (Matthew 10:23)

*I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13)

Daniel keeps the word like, one like the Son of Adam, and that fits the one who took on flesh and came to resemble the sons of Adam. Yahusha (Jesus) takes the name from the vision and uses it for himself. Then he says what the coming looks like.

*And then shall appear the sign of the Son of Adam in heaven: and then shall all the tribes of the earth mourn, and they shall see the Son of Adam coming in the clouds of heaven with power and great glory.* (Matthew 24:30)

*For the Son of Adam shall come in the glory of his Father with his angels; and then he shall reward every man according to his works.* (Matthew 16:27)

So the going over the cities of Yashar'el (Israel) is not an errand that ends in a season. It is a standing errand, carried from city to city while the scattered are gathered, and it runs until the day he is seen coming with power. On that day the reward follows the works.
